basic_information.short_title: Datu Blah Sinsuat District Hospital Upgrading Act of 2022
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE EXISTING DATU BLAH SINSUAT DISTRICT HOSPITAL IN MAGUINDANAO FROM ITS PRESENT LEVEL I WITH A TEN (10) BED CAPACITY INTO LEVEL II WITH AN AUTHORIZED ONE HUNDRED (100) BED CAPACITY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Upgrades the Datu Blah Sinsuat District Hospital in Maguindanao from a 10-bed Level I facility to a Level II hospital with 100 authorised beds — a tenfold increase in capacity.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Section 22, Article IX of the Organic Law obliges the region to provide comprehensive and integrated health service delivery and to establish a general hospital system by law, so that the basic right to life is attainable through prompt, excellent and affordable medical services.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: The hospital moves from Level I to Level II under national Department of Health standards. Buildings, medical and office equipment, other facilities, operating funds and personnel are all upgraded to match, including the construction and procurement needed to meet the standard.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of Datu Blah Sinsuat and surrounding areas in Maguindanao
Patients who previously had to travel for Level II services
Hospital staff, whose posts and funding are upgraded
PhilHealth members, since the hospital must integrate the Universal Health Care Act
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2022. Delivery depends on the annual Bangsamoro budget.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. Your district hospital is authorised to grow from 10 beds to 100 and from Level I to Level II — more services, more staff, more equipment.
in_practice: Level I (10 beds) becomes Level II (100 authorised beds)
Level II means a broader range of services under national DOH standards
Buildings, equipment, operating funds and personnel are upgraded with it
The hospital integrates the Universal Health Care Act into its operations
The Ministry of Health supervises and sets the organisational structure

for_specific_groups.Patients: A Level II hospital offers more than a Level I — the upgrade is about what can be treated locally rather than referred away.
for_specific_groups.Hospital staff: Personnel are expressly upgraded along with the facility.
for_specific_groups.PhilHealth members: Section 4 requires the hospital to integrate all relevant provisions of the Universal Health Care Act.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2022; actual construction and staffing depend on annual appropriations.
what_you_can_do: Ask the Ministry of Health about the implementing rules — the act required them within 60 days of enactment
Ask what stage the upgrade has reached; the act sets no completion deadline
watch_out_for: The act names no peso amount — funding is 'from the Bangsamoro General Appropriations' and 'such amount as may be needed'.
There is no deadline for completing the upgrade and no reporting requirement.
An authorised bed capacity is a legal ceiling, not a built one.

key_terms_explained.Level I hospital: A basic facility — emergency care, general medicine, a small ward.
key_terms_explained.Level II hospital: A larger facility with specialist departments and services a Level I cannot provide.
key_terms_explained.Authorized bed capacity: The number of beds the hospital is legally allowed to operate, which may exceed what is built.
key_terms_explained.UHC Act: Republic Act 11223, the national Universal Health Care law.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Dhu Al-Qa'dah 16, 1443 / 15 June 2022, approved by the Chief Minister on 12 July 2022.

benefits.headline: A tenfold bed increase and a step up to Level II services.

direct_benefits.benefit: Level II services closer to home
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Residents of Datu Blah Sinsuat and nearby areas

indirect_benefits: Universal Health Care coverage integrated into hospital operations
limitations: Authorised capacity is not the same as operating capacity.

for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on the public.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Health – BARMM, which has administrative supervision and approves the organisational structure
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A patient in Datu Blah Sinsuat previously referred to Cotabato City for a service a Level II hospital provides should, once the upgrade is delivered, be treated locally.
A resident asks why the hospital still has fewer than 100 beds. The act authorises the capacity; building it depends on the annual budget, and no deadline is set.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Datu Blah Sinsuat District Hospital Upgrading Act of 2022”.

Section 2 — Policy grounded on Section 22, Article IX of the Organic Law (RA 11054): comprehensive and integrated health service delivery, a general hospital system established by law, and the basic right to life made attainable through prompt intervention of excellent and affordable medical services.

Section 3 — Upgrades the existing Level I hospital with a 10-bed capacity into a Level II hospital with 100 authorised beds, in accordance with national standards of the Bureau of Health Facilities and Services under the Department of Health. Existing buildings including landscaping, medical and office equipment and other facilities, together with operating funds and personnel, are upgraded to include the construction and procurement needed to meet the prescribed standards.
Section 4 — The hospital shall integrate into its operations all relevant provisions of Republic Act 11223, the Universal Health Care Act.
Section 5 — The hospital is under the administrative supervision of the Ministry of Health, which determines and approves the organisational structure.

Section 6 — Funding is appropriated from the Bangsamoro General Appropriations for the upgrading, including construction of infrastructure, acquisition of medical and office equipment, and the annual budget for personnel services, maintenance and operations, and thereafter such amount as may be needed for continued operations.
Section 7 — MOH-BARMM shall promulgate implementing rules within 60 days after enactment.
Section 9 — Repeals inconsistent BARMM laws, including those passed under the defunct ARMM, on the operations and upgrading of this hospital.
Section 10 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

citizen_questions.a: The hospital moves from Level I to Level II under national DOH standards, and from 10 beds to 100 authorised beds — meaning more services can be given locally rather than referred elsewhere.
The act names no amount. It appropriates funding 'from the Bangsamoro General Appropriations' and thereafter such amount as may be needed.

citizen_questions.q: When will the upgrade be finished?
citizen_questions.a: The act sets no deadline. It required implementing rules from the Ministry of Health within 60 days of enactment, but no completion date for the works.
No. It is the authorised capacity — the legal ceiling. Actual beds depend on construction funded through the annual budget.
